one-color-places.title: Sunflower Keys — Trace one note color through three spatial orders
notes: Six Moss seeds travel outward in Drawn order. Their note color is the same; only places change.
The same six Moss seeds travel inward in Drawn order. This is not a falling pitch scale.
The same six Moss seeds alternate inner and outer places in Drawn order. Planting stays silent.
one-color-places.facts: All seeds are unique and modulo5=4 (Moss). Same six-seed set in every row, constant pitch color; physical positions differ. No equal-loudness claim.

two-color-edges.title: Sunflower Keys — Put the same two note colors into a call an answer and a braid
rows: Three low notes then three high
Three high notes then three low
notes: Drawn plays three first-color notes then three fifth-color notes. The high group visits its outer place first.
Drawn starts with three fifth-color notes then answers with three first-color notes. The six places are unchanged.
Drawn alternates first and fifth note colors across the same six places. No new timing or voices are added.
two-color-edges.facts: Modulo5 gives three color0 and three color4 seeds. All rows have set0,4,5,9,10,14; fixed cardinality6. Drawn matters; Up follows the ordinary order instead.

two-arches.title: Sunflower Keys — Answer one five-color arch with another
notes: Drawn rises through five colors, then falls through the second five places. All ten seeds remain distinct.
Drawn interleaves the rising inner arch and falling outer arch. This changes order, not note duration.
Drawn makes two rising five-color calls. The same ten seeds and all five colors remain.
two-arches.facts: Each set is0..9 with each modulo5 color twice. First two rows preserve internally ordered subsequences0..4 and9..5, while third reverses second arch. No octave claim.
